card.name: Re- and causal verbs before adverse events
card.fires_on: The re- start of words like rechallenge, reactivation, reevaluation, rejection, and causal verbs like induce or produce. It appears in drug-label text where the next piece completes the word or names an adverse effect.

modes.label: Re- word starts
modes.description: The re- opening of a longer word, often a medical term like rechallenge or reactivation.
modes.example: Infections and<< re>>activation of infections have been reported.

modes.label: Causal verbs
modes.description: Verbs meaning to cause, placed right before an adverse effect.
modes.example: Disopyramide causes QT prolongation which could<< induce>> arrhythmia.

card.writes: It seems to push toward word endings and outcome-type words like led, marked, and scenario, though the effect is weak.
card.plain: It fires on the start of re- words, and on verbs like induce or produce that lead into a side effect.
